prompt:
You judge OPENING clips for 60-second videos made of other channels' own words (each clip is a person's
own words from a show). Each candidate below would play FIRST, before anything else is said. Judge each one ALONE, as
the opener of a video; the candidates are not compared with each other and never play together.

CANDIDATE id="b3ad2b8356e4a8d70dd9" (on screen: TFTC): "I think one of the best starting points is January 1st, 2023. The bottom of the 22 bear market, which wasn't a Bitcoin bear market. It was a global bear market. Bonds lost 50 % of their value. TLT went down 50%."
CANDIDATE id="704fa6e1af4a86ff1d07" (on screen: Coin Bureau): "On the 29th of October, Binance's hot wallets gave up Ethereum, Bitcoin, USDT, USDC, about 233 million XRP, and a long tail of smaller tokens. The total was about $6.3 billion worth."

For EACH candidate: THE HOOK is judged on its own job, NOT on the through-line. Rate each of its three parts 1-5 separately:
   "scroll": do its first 2-3 seconds stop a viewer from scrolling past? (5 = certainly, 1 = not at all)
   "alone": does it stand alone, so that a viewer needs nothing said before it? (5 = fully, 1 = not at all)
   "setup": does it set up what follows, so that a viewer who hears it wants the next clip? (5 = certainly, 1 = not
   at all)
Give "why": a few words on the candidate's weakest part.
Return ONLY this JSON object: {"hooks": {"b3ad2b8356e4a8d70dd9": {"scroll": 1, "alone": 1, "setup": 1, "why": "..."}, "704fa6e1af4a86ff1d07": {"scroll": 1, "alone": 1, "setup": 1, "why": "..."}}}
text: {"hooks": {"b3ad2b8356e4a8d70dd9": {"scroll": 2, "alone": 3, "setup": 3, "why": "'I think one of the best starting points' is a soft, mid-thought opener that reads as someone already deep in a conversation, not a hook."}, "704fa6e1af4a86ff1d07": {"scroll": 4, "alone": 5, "setup": 4, "why": "The statement is a complete factual summary; the dramatic $6.3B loss grabs attention but the clip resolves itself, slightly reducing the pull toward the next clip."}}}
